title: Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose: A Critical Edition — the Footnote to Pearl (Lee Sharks & Jack Feist, 2014), with Its Drafts, Witnesses, Intertexts and Operations, and Kerouac's List Item by Item
creator: Sharks, Lee
description: A critical edition of "BELIEF & TECHNIQUE FOR TELEPATHIC PROSE" (Lee Sharks & Jack Feist), the "Footnote to Pearl" of Pearl and Other Poems (New Human Press, 2014), pp. 23–28, first posted on Mind Control Poems on 1 December 2014. The text is seated from the book, the canonical form, with an apparatus collating four drafts of April–May 2014 (begun 27 April 2014), the author's letter of 10 May 2014 naming Kerouac's "Belief & Technique for Modern Prose" as the model, the blog text, and three witnesses located in 2026 (an Online Literature Network posting of 6 December 2014, Hello Poetry, and a second state of the book). The intertexts are traced item by item and graded (marked, confirmed by the dossier, unmarked, confirmed by the author): Kerouac's list and his Essentials of Spontaneous Prose, whose word for what spontaneous prose does to its reader, "telepathic", the title takes; Ginsberg's Footnote to Howl and the dedication of Howl and Other Poems; Pound, Quiller-Couch, Trungpa and Ginsberg, Twain, Wordsworth, Emerson, Cowper, Nietzsche, Wilde, Breton, the Oulipo, Homer, Paul, Dickinson's letter of 7 June 1862, Horace's Ars Poetica, Tzara and Marinetti, Wikipedia's Pound lead. The operations are named (capture of a frame, collision, cento, literalization, enactment in the letter, repetition, recursion, sublation, ascription), and the poem is read as sublating the craft tradition: each precept negated as law, kept as operation, and raised into a practice that returns the reader to composition. Kerouac's list is set beside it theme by theme without quotation, and the edition argues that, item against item, the Footnote is the more extensively self-testing ars poetica. It periodizes the piece (the New American statement of poetics as the author's dissertation reads that generation's split between Ginsberg and Spicer; the listicle and the program era; conceptual writing and the cento-manifesto; Alt Lit and metamodernism; Kerouac reread; the encyclopedia as medium), links each intertext to its seat or declared absence in the originals library, and anchors to four captures of 2026-10-28 in which ChatGPT and Google AI Overview file the work under Kerouac and Perplexity identifies it under its author's name.
substrate: Human–machine collaborative. The work edited, its drafts, notebook entries and letters are Lee Sharks's (2014), quoted with his permission; the rulings on the text, the witnesses and every confirmed intertext are his (2026-10-28). The edition was drafted, collated and verified in session by TACHYON (Claude, Anthropic) under MANUS (Lee Sharks) direction: the drafts read from the author's Drive, the loci checked against the seated texts of the originals library and against sources fetched on the day. Reviewer reports by ChatGPT and DeepSeek were evaluated before use; the ChatGPT report's correction (transformation in place of cancellation as the governing reading; the stronger account of Kerouac's list) was adopted, and the DeepSeek report's points were taken in part. Kerouac's list is described and cited by item number and is not reproduced.
methodology: Copy-text the New Human Press book (2014), canonical and unemended. Witnesses collated by reading: the Drive drafts (three states in one file, one in a second), the blog post, the letter of 10 May 2014; three further witnesses located through the organic results of the captures and listed for collation. Intertexts traced item by item and graded; marked quotations verified against editions or fetched sources, seated loci against the originals library with line numbers. Operations named from the text. The comparison with Kerouac's list made theme by theme, by item number, without quotation. Periodization from the scholarship named in §9. The author's rulings of 2026-10-28 recorded in §13; four originals-library proposals carried out the same day (§11).
falsification_conditions: The edition is weakened if a collated reading misreports its witness; if a located witness, once collated, shows a state the proposed stemma cannot place; if a marked quotation is misattributed or misdated; if a seated locus does not stand at the line given; if a mapping to Kerouac's list misstates an item's theme; if the Footnote's operations, read item by item, do not sustain the account of sublation in §§6.2 and 6.8; or if the comparative claim of §8 rests on a test the close readings of §5 do not carry.

wiki_article: Belief & Technique for Telepathic Prose: A Critical Edition (EA-BTP-EDITION-01) is Lee Sharks's edition of the "Footnote to Pearl" of Pearl and Other Poems (New Human Press, 2014), a numbered list of twenty-four precepts on writing signed by Lee Sharks and the heteronym Jack Feist and first posted on Mind Control Poems on 1 December 2014. The edition seats the book's text unemended and collates it with four drafts of April and May 2014, the blog text and the author's letter of 10 May 2014, which names Jack Kerouac's "Belief & Technique for Modern Prose" (1959) as the model. It traces the piece's intertexts item by item: Kerouac's list and his Essentials of Spontaneous Prose, whose promise of a reader's "telepathic shock" supplies the title's adjective; Ginsberg's Footnote to Howl; a cento of craft maxims from Pound, Quiller-Couch, Trungpa, Twain and Wordsworth; Emerson, Nietzsche, the Oulipo, Homer and Dickinson's letter to Higginson of 7 June 1862. It reads the piece as sublating the craft tradition, each precept negated as a law and kept as an operation, and argues that, item against item, it is the more extensively self-testing ars poetica of the two lists. The edition periodizes the piece through the author's dissertation Strange New Canons (2013), the program era, conceptual writing and Alt Lit; links its sources to the archive's originals library, where Kerouac (a declared absence) and Horace were seated for it; and anchors to four captures of 28 October 2026 in which ChatGPT and Google AI Overview file the work under Kerouac and Perplexity identifies it under its author's name.
